Wait, what about parental leave? Are we supposed to justify it or argue against it? I think it should be a voluntary workplace benefit; it's not fair to force everyone to pay into a tax system only for young married men and women to leave work to raise their nth newborn child. for those companies who are very well organized and have the cash to pay for group benefits, leave it up to them to offer it to their employees. It should be determined on an individual basis, I don't think the government should do more meddling

I am entertaining the idea of a living basic income. In this model the parents would be able to take as much paid leave as they'd want to, whenever they wanted to. It's for a different world than today though, and a lot would have to evolve in our culture for such a thing to work.

My last employer made a great point about maternity leave: in most companies if a mother stays away for months the manager has to hire a substitute for the time being and by the time the mother comes back she has become the substitute and is likely to be fired as soon as possible. I mean, if someone is doing your job for months it's their job now. Sad but true.

As an employer myself this would be a hard decision to make. I guess I would use local law as the guideline and try to adapt it on a case-by-case basis, trying to balance the needs of the company and the parents. I don't like having to ad-lib stuff like this though and would much rather have better guidelines to start with. As I mention above the current laws here are lackluster.

Anyway just my uneducated opinion, haven't read any of your references or thought much about that up until now.
